passages.note: Roll call 305 shows Soliday in the Yea list on final House passage of SB 101, 63-31, not near-unanimous.

passages.provision_quote: (b) A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: Enrolled SB 101 text lets a person claim a religious-exercise exemption from any burdening law absent strict scrutiny, with no carve-out for anti-discrimination law.

rows.reasoning: Soliday voted Yea on SB 101 (2015), a single-subject religious freedom restoration act whose operative text lets a person assert a substantial burden on their religious exercise as a claim or defense unless the government shows a compelling interest met by the least restrictive means, with no carve-out preserving anti-discrimination protections. That matches the rung text 'protect religious freedom and allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs,' and excludes rung 2's carve-out language and rung 5's organizational-hiring-autonomy clause.
